descriptionChirho: Noun feminine שִׁקְמָה (shiqmah), collective/plural שִׁקְמִים: the sycamore-fig tree (Ficus sycomorus), a large, shade-giving tree common in the lowlands of ancient Israel, valued for its timber and fruit though inferior to the cedar. Used as a marker of abundance and commonness: cedars replaced sycamores in Solomon's prosperity (1 Kgs 10:27; 2 Chr 1:15, 9:27), sycamores destroyed by frost as divine judgment on Egypt (Ps 78:47), sycamores cut down but arrogantly replaced with cedars in Israel's hubris (Isa 9:10), and Amos's occupation as a sycamore-dresser (Amos 7:14). Also mentioned as part of David's estate overseen by Baal-Hanan (1 Chr 27:28). Arabic جُمَّيْز (jummayz, the standard Arabic word for sycamore-fig), Korean 뽕나무/떡나무/돌무화과나무 (various Korean tree names showing translators' difficulty finding an exact equivalent), Spanish sicomoro, Hindi गूलर (gular, the Indian fig species used as equivalent). All five auto-clusters represent the same botanical referent, split only by prepositional and conjunctive prefixes.
